issues.legal_issue: The court fee payable for a partition claim depends on the plaintiff’s pleaded joint possession and request for partition and separate possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff alleged in the plaint that she was in joint possession of the properties.
She sought partition and separate possession of her half share as an heir.
She paid court fee under Section 37(2) of the applicable State Act, but the fee was challenged.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the fee payable was the fee claimed under Section 37(2), allowed the appeal, and remitted the suit for expeditious proceedings. Its decision did not determine the merits, including the validity of the will.
issues.legal_principle: Section 37(2) of the State Act applied to the pleaded claim and corresponded to Article 17(b) of the Central Act, the predecessor legislation. Court-fee provisions that restrict access to justice should be strictly construed; where there is reasonable doubt, the benefit goes to the person claiming that the lower fee is payable. Courts should focus on the real issues rather than peripheral disputes.

predicates.partition_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking partition of property.
predicates.joint_possession_pleaded: The plaintiff alleged that they were in joint possession of the property.
predicates.separate_possession_sought: The plaintiff sought separate possession of their share of the property.
predicates.lower_partition_court_fee_applies: The lower court fee applicable to a partition claim based on joint possession is payable.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff in a partition suit pleads joint possession and seeks separate possession of a share, the lower partition court fee applies.
